A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoWorld and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. Inspection included v1 Appendices A-B. v2 incorporates Appendix A's discard-ratio study into Section 4.5 and has no separate appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2-4.3 and Appendix A report original benchmark results, component ablations and generated-scene examples.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds geometry-consistency tests, conditioning ablations and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The two-stage generation procedure, VGGT geometry features, alignment loss, adaptation module, 50% token removal and cross-attention fusion remain unchanged. Explicit two-stage terminology and the additional conditioning ablations do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DL3DV and evaluate on RealEstate10K and Tanks and Temples for camera-controlled novel-view synthesis and 3D scene generation. The new geometry measurements evaluate these existing outputs; the omitted example galleries do not establish a distinct change in task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1-2 replace DimensionX with Hunyuan-Voyager, and Table 2 adds ViewCrafter to the 3D scene generation comparison. See3D and FlexWorld remain, while ViewCrafter was already evaluated for novel-view synthesis. This is a focused update to the comparator sets.

E3.justification: Sections 4.3-4.5 add adjacent-frame MEt3R evaluation on 49-frame 3DGS renderings, two-view MASt3R matching, no-geometry and depth-only controls, and computational-cost evaluation with specified hardware and method-specific output sizes. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Existing Section 4.1 training budgets, sampling procedures and standard benchmark metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct tests of removing geometric conditioning and replacing it with depth maps (Figure 8), plus multi-view consistency and image-matching analyses (Figures 6-7). These directly examine the geometric benefits of the method. Existing component, training-duration and token-weighting analyses remain; the discard-ratio study moves from Appendix A into Section 4.5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. The new per-frame MEt3R curves show variation across frames, not repeated-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Shared benchmark and numerical ablation values remain unchanged, including GeoWorld's RealEstate10K PSNR of 17.28 in Table 1. v2 adds Hunyuan-Voyager results, ViewCrafter reconstruction results, MEt3R curves, matching counts including 1250 for GeoWorld, and cost measurements. DimensionX results and the additional appendix galleries are removed, substantially changing the reported evidence.

T1.justification: Equations 1-4 retain the same diffusion loss, geometric feature loss, combined objective and cross-attention formulation. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the new evaluation measures introduce no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v2 adds computational efficiency as a headline contribution, claiming approximately 0.3 times the parameters and 7.5 times faster inference than Hunyuan-Voyager. It also narrows v1's blanket quantitative-superiority claim to superior fidelity and competitive perceptual quality. The central full-frame geometry contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets lower MEt3R scores as evidence of stable 3DGS structures with fewer geometric conflicts, and matching counts as evidence of pixel-level geometric consistency. It also discusses GPU-memory overhead from loading VGGT. Existing explanations concerning imperfect conditioning and token filtering largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents simultaneous training of the adaptation and diffusion modules, inference output sizes, GPU memory capacities, parameter accounting and total two-stage timing. These are additional disclosures, not demonstrated changes to existing settings. v1 Appendix B's supplementary-video filenames are omitted; the project-page address remains equivalent.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to MEt3R, Depth Anything 3, WorldMirror and newer video world models, and emphasizes efficiency relative to Hunyuan-Voyager. The related-work taxonomy and core geometry-guidance positioning remain. Voyager was already cited in v1, although it was not an evaluated baseline.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, central introduction passages, contribution statements and conclusion are substantially rewritten around full-frame conditioning and two-stage efficiency. The experimental narrative is reorganized, Appendix A is integrated into the main text, and Appendix B is removed. Most methodological prose remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 changes the predominantly two-column layout to a single-column format, redraws the pipeline comparison in Figure 2, revises qualitative comparison panels and adds geometry-analysis figures and a cost table. Existing ablations are relocated and reformatted, while the additional appendix galleries disappear.

improvement.justification: The new geometry diagnostics and conditioning controls strengthen evidence for the central mechanism, while updated baselines and narrower performance claims improve the comparison. The gain is limited by the illustrative scope of the new geometry tests and removal of extra appendix examples. Cost reporting adds transparency, but its broad efficiency claim needs qualification: Table 3 uses unequal output sizes and lists ViewCrafter at 2.6B parameters versus GeoWorld's 3.9B.
